prompt: Some people think that good health is very important to every person, so medical service should not be run by profit-making companies. Do the advantages of private health care outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
It is widely argued that good health is essential for everyone, and that healthcare services should not be controlled by private companies for profit. Although private healthcare has disadvantages, I believe that its advantages considerably outweigh its disadvantages in terms of finance and time.

One of the main advantages of private healthcare is that it can provide better-quality medical services. As private clinics compete to attract more patients, they try to improve their services, hire experienced doctors and use modern medical equipment. For example, private hospitals may invest cutting-edge technologies and specialists to provide better treatment. Another important benefit is that patients usually have shorter waiting times. Unlike public hospitals, private clinics often have fewer patients and more flexible appointment systems. For instance, a patient may be able to see a doctor within a few days at a private clinic, while they may have to wait much longer at a public hospital. Therefore, private healthcare can provide patients with better services and faster access to medical treatment.

On the other hand, private healthcare can be more expensive than public healthcare. Private clinics usually charge higher fees because they need to make a profit. As a result, people with low incomes may not be able to afford these services. For example, a patient who needs expensive surgery may have to pay a large amount of money at a private hospital, while the same treatment may cost much less in a public hospital.

In conclusion, while private healthcare is more expensive, I believe that its advantages outweigh its disadvantages because it offers better services and shorter waiting times. Despite costing more than public clinics.
